Text: The femur's sharp ridge (the linea aspera) runs down its {{c1::posterior::anterior or posterior}} side, but the tibia's sharp ridge runs down its {{c1::anterior::anterior or posterior}} side.
Back Extra:
Why: the femur's ridge runs down the back of the shaft and anchors thigh muscles (chiefly the adductors), while the tibia's sharp front border is the bare bone of the shin.

Pitfall: the two long bones are opposite, so a sharp ridge tells you front from back only once you know which bone you hold.
